title: Extract universal style-testing core from style-rspec
description:
## Why (Computational)

style-rspec is the only style skill in this workbench with no universal core beneath it. Every
other language style skill (style-python, style-rails, style-frontend, style-swift) sits on top of
hooks/style-core.md and carries only its language deltas. Test-writing guidance is therefore
Rails-only: anyone working in Jest, Vitest, pytest, or XCTest gets nothing from this repo, even
though most of what makes a good unit test (one behavior per test, arrange-act-assert, determinism,
what not to test) is framework-independent. The stakeholder is anyone using this workbench outside a
Rails repo, which covers most of the languages it claims to support.

## Estimated size
5 files, ~290 LOC, band: Target. New SKILL.md ~220 LOC, style-rspec trim ~60 LOC, 3 registration lines.
design:
Mirror the established delta structure rather than genericizing style-rspec. Extract the
framework-independent principles into a new skills/style-testing/SKILL.md, and rewrite style-rspec to
carry only RSpec/Rails deltas (let/let!/subject, request-vs-controller specs, factories,
describe/context nesting), opening with an explicit pointer to the core the way style-python points at
style-core.

Key decision: do NOT make style-rspec framework-agnostic. Its opinionated Rails specifics are the
value, and `let` has no Jest equivalent, so genericizing would delete the sharpest guidance and leave
platitudes. Framework deltas for Vitest/Jest/pytest become sibling skills later, once a real second
consumer exists (wait for duplication before abstracting).
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given a reader opens skills/style-testing/SKILL.md, when they scan it end to end, then no rule names an RSpec, Rails, Jest, Vitest, or pytest construct.
2. Given a reader opens skills/style-rspec/SKILL.md, when they read its opening section, then it names style-testing as the core it extends.
3. Given `grep -rw style-testing AGENTS.md README.md .claude-plugin/plugin.json`, when run, then all three files match.
4. Given review-rails/SKILL.md line 30 defers to style-rspec, when style-rspec has been rewritten as a delta, then that reference still resolves to an existing skill.
5. Given the orphan check in /validate-plugin, when run after the change, then style-testing has at least one referrer among skills/, agents/, or commands/ (style-rspec at minimum).
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)
- skills/style-testing/SKILL.md exists and contains only framework-independent guidance.
- style-rspec retains no guidance that would apply unchanged to Jest or pytest.
- style-rspec opens with an explicit pointer to style-testing as the core it extends.
- style-testing is registered in .claude-plugin/plugin.json, AGENTS.md, and README.md.
- review-rails' existing deferral to style-rspec still resolves.
